ground_truth_explanation:
Stipulated in the Austrian Framework for Open Government Platforms and the White Paper of the Cooperation OGD Austria, referring to the Open Principles and the Creative Commons Licence CC-BY 4.0. (https://www.data.gv.at/anleitung)

response to reviewers:

It refers to the Open Principles and the Creative Commons Licence CC-BY 4.0. Specifically, open data reuse is defined as the use of data that is freely available to everyone to use, modify, and share for any purpose—subject to the terms specified under the Creative Commons Licence CC-BY 4.0. (Source: data.gv.at)

Is there a national open data policy in your country and, if your country is an EU Member State, does this include a national legislation for the transposition of the Open Data Directive?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide (1) the URL and (2) title of the policy document and (3) briefly describe.
* If ‘other’, please provide (1) a brief explanation to support your answer choice and (2) provide the URL and indicate the policy section which explicitly references open data.
ground_truth_explanation:
o Basis: Federal Act on the Re-Use of Public Sector Information 2022 (Informationsweiterverwendungsgesetz – IWG 2022). https://www.ris.bka.gv.at/GeltendeFassung.wxe?Abfrage=Bundesnormen&Gesetzesnummer=20011973
o Responsible authority for the implementation of the Open Data Directive 2019/1024 & IWG 2022: Federal Chancellery of Austria (BKA)
o Responsible authority for the national data portal: Federal Chancellery of Austria (BKA)
o The Cooperation Open Government Data (OGD) Austria perpetuates open data governance at all levels (federal-regional-local) within the Austrian public sector
(https://www.data.gv.at/infos/cooperation-ogd-austria/)
generated_justification:
Yes, Austria has a national open data policy framework that includes formal national legislation for the transposition of the EU Open Data Directive (Directive (EU) 2019/1024).

1. Legal and Policy Basis: The Open Data and PSI Directive (EU) 2019/1024 has been transposed at the federal level in Austria through the Informationsweiterverwendungsgesetz 2022 (Information Reuse Act 2022, IWG 2022). This law mandates public sector bodies to enable reuse of their data sets for commercial and non-commercial purposes, aligning closely with the EU directive's provisions. Furthermore, implementation occurs at both federal and regional levels (the so-called 9+1 rule), ensuring comprehensive application of the directive throughout the country.

2. Governance and Implementation: Open data sets considered "high value datasets" (HVD) under the EU directive are required to be made available as open data via Austria's national data portal (data.gv.at). The portal and supporting official guideline documents provide a structured approach for public entities to publish data openly while respecting data protection constraints, such as anonymization measures.

3. References to Documentation: The national guideline "Ein Leitfaden für offene Daten" (https://www.data.gv.at/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Open_Data_Leitfaden_20230622.pdf) explicitly discusses the legal framework referencing the EU Open Data Directive. Additionally, the overview on Weiterverwendung von Daten und Dokumenten at https://www.usp.gv.at/themen/betrieb-und-umwelt/laufender-betrieb/weitere-informationen-laufender-betrieb/informationsweiterverwendung.html details the legal basis grounded in the IWG 2022 as the implementation vehicle for the Open Data Directive.

These elements collectively confirm Austria's formal national open data policy and legislation for the EU directive’s transposition, thereby fulfilling the question requirements comprehensively.

2. This collaboration fosters participation from a range of actors including administration, economy, and society, ensuring that their perspectives contribute to open data policies and implementation.

3. This approach ensures inclusive stakeholder engagement, transparent processes, and a culture of trust and collaboration between political, administrative actors, and the public, as described in the “Grünbuch: Partizipation im digitalen Zeitalter” (Green Paper on Participation in the Digital Age) (S3, S5).

This creates stable and traceable processes for continuous improvement and greater inclusivity (S3, S5).

This definition is similar to the PSI Directive definition : « Public sector bodies collect, produce, reproduce and disseminate documents in order to fulfill their public service mission. The use of these documents for other purposes constitutes reuse ».

Besides that definition, more restrictive approaches have also emerged : some consider that only perennial uses of data are reuses while others consider any use of data as reuse. In our day to day operations, any exploitation of data in order to obtain information is considered as reuse, whether this exploitation is freely accessible or not : following that definition, a use of private data or a data journalist’s work to prepare for an investigation will be considered as reuse.
